response.markdown_report:
The best initial experiment is **stochastic recent-prefix training**: train the corrected GRU4Rec on either the complete observed prefix or its recent suffix, retaining the same immediate next-item target.

Starting-point insights: (1) stale-interest recommendations motivate reducing dependence on old events; (2) weak connections to recent activity motivate learning from recent evidence; (3) Electronics’ 9.7% wrong-order rate identifies a separation problem; (4) mapped embedding similarities near 0.5 do not support a collapse penalty. These observations motivate an experiment, not an established causal explanation.

Related-work insights: (1) UFRec changes training supervision while preserving deployed scoring; (2) PinnerFormer shows the usefulness of broader future supervision, although persistent interests may conflict with immediate intent here; (3) official GRU4Rec makes objective choice a credible alternative; (4) sampled-metric analysis limits conclusions to the pinned evaluation protocol. None establishes that prefix cropping improves this benchmark.

The framework separates three directions: **context exposure** changes observed histories, **supervision horizon** changes training targets, and **ranking objective** changes competition between candidates. All retain one causal GRU and one checkpoint per category.

Three atomic proposals follow. Scores list originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Proposal | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-prefix training | 3/6/8/6/3 | A small training intervention directly tests stale-interest and recent-context dependence. | Familiar sequence augmentation can erase useful persistent preferences; separation gains are uncertain. |
| Low-weight two-step auxiliary prediction [UFRec] | 3/6/5/6/5 | Additional training signal could improve sparse representations without inference overhead. | Longer-horizon targets may dilute immediate intent and reinforce older interests. |
| Corrected sampled softmax [official GRU4Rec; LogQ paper] | 2/7/4/8/5 | Directly changes discrimination among sampled alternatives. | Requires exact proposal probabilities and only indirectly addresses user complaints. |

Select recent-prefix training at 0% progress because it introduces no inference parameters and offers a bounded, attributable comparison. It explicitly targets **revived older interests** and **recommendations weakly connected to recent activity**. Its model-facing hypothesis is reduced wrong-order frequency through better recent-context representations, especially in Electronics; this remains unverified.

For each sampled training row, extract valid observed events. With probability 0.25, retain a uniformly selected suffix length between min(5,n) and n; otherwise retain the complete prefix. Left-pad again and preserve the original immediate target. Use one final-position loss per row in both intervention and matched control, preventing supervision-density differences from confounding cropping.

Compare the matched full-prefix control with cropping using unchanged macro validation HR@10. Keep seeds, routing, training limits, evaluator and checkpoint schedule fixed. Report diagnostic margins and wrong-order rates without selecting on them. Cropping cannot establish compatibility, redundancy, mood or quantities. No experiment was executed.

idea.description: Stochastic recent-prefix training for the corrected GRU4Rec: occasionally remove older observed events while retaining the immediate next-item target. Train one jointly optimized GRU model per category; deploy its ordinary scoring head without augmentation or score fusion.
idea.motivation: The supplied user diagnosis identifies revived older interests and weak connections to recent activity. Training on occasional recent suffixes may make the GRU less dependent on distant context when recent evidence is sufficient. Electronics’ measured 9.7% sampled wrong-order rate supplies a model-facing target, but neither that rate nor the qualitative feedback establishes that distant context caused the failures. This is a controlled hypothesis rather than a claimed improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
The actual corrected baseline source is absent from the supplied material, so this is an implementation specification rather than a fabricated train.py replacement. Modify its family-specific sampler and loss-position mask; preserve its GRU architecture, scoring head, optimizer, dropout, clipping and predictor writer.

Define an example using a training-history target index j >= 1. Its input comprises only observed events before j, truncated by the baseline maximum sequence length, and its target is history[j]. Retain the baseline distribution over users and target indices. If the baseline provides dense targets, explicitly switch BOTH the matched control and intervention to a single final-position target; do not compare cropping against dense supervision and attribute the whole difference to augmentation. This supervision change itself may affect results relative to the supplied baseline, and must be reported.

Intervention: independently for each row, draw a Bernoulli(0.25). When selected, draw integer k uniformly from min(5,n) through n inclusive, where n is the number of observed input events; retain the last k events. Otherwise keep all n events. Histories of five or fewer events are unchanged. Left-pad the resulting sequence. Never insert the target into the input or use held-out interactions. Report the actual fraction shortened because the chosen suffix may equal the full prefix. Use the existing negative sampler and baseline loss on the retained final target; do not introduce hard mining, an auxiliary objective or text features in this first trial.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, the four supplied categories, maximum epochs 200, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and the supplied validation/checkpoint schedule. Respect the host SASREC_EPOCHS setting within the maximum. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU per trial and account for all executed training, debugging and diagnostics within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not read other trials, reuse their checkpoints, fetch weights or inspect hidden tests.

Inference uses the full supplied observed history with the baseline maximum-length truncation. Cropping is training-only. Padding must not update recurrent state, and readout must gather the maximum nonzero position, never count-1. Preserve baseline empty-history behavior. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items). Because architecture remains unchanged, the predictor writer should serialize and reconstruct the unchanged architecture and selected checkpoint; verify fresh-predictor scores match in-memory scores. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Controls are alternative experiments and are never combined at inference.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model remains the actual GRU module. Preserve the host ModelView and loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. For matched diagnostics, place the immediate target and negative at the final valid input position and zero-mask other targets in both conditions. Compute margins through the actual model interfaces and state the final-position population in their definitions. Do not directly compare these aggregates with earlier dense-position diagnostics as if their populations matched. Keep unavailable metadata category breakdowns explicitly unavailable.

A bounded initial sequence is the supplied corrected baseline, the matched full-prefix/final-target control, and the cropped/final-target intervention. The latter contrast isolates cropping conditional on the altered supervision scheme. Select only on pinned macro validation HR@10 and log per-category effects. Full-catalog recommendations for the twenty training users use the same single model and existing unseen-item filtering. Interpret simulator feedback qualitatively. No validation gain, full-catalog improvement or recovery of actual intent is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
def prepare_training_row(history, target_index, maxlen, crop, rng):
    # target_index and user selection follow the baseline training sampler.
    target = history[target_index]
    observed = history[max(0, target_index - maxlen):target_index]
    assert len(observed) > 0
    if crop and rng.random() < 0.25:
        n = len(observed)
        k = rng.randint(min(5, n), n + 1)  # exclusive upper bound
        observed = observed[-k:]
    sequence = left_pad(observed, maxlen, padding_id=0)
    positive = zeros(maxlen)
    negative = zeros(maxlen)
    last = maximum_index_where(sequence != 0)
    positive[last] = target
    negative[last] = unchanged_baseline_negative_sampler(target)
    return sequence, positive, negative

# Run matched control and cropping as separate trials, never fuse them.
for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
    seed_training(42)
    model = supplied_corrected_GRU4Rec(resolved_baseline_config)
    for epoch in range(min(resolved_host_epochs, 200)):
        for step in range(200):
            sequence, positive, negative = matched_family_sample_batch(crop=trial_crop)
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            valid_targets = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0)
            loss = baseline_loss(features, positive, negative, mask=valid_targets)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
        unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint(category)
write_predictor_using_identical_baseline_architecture_and_routing()

# Inference: no cropping, no auxiliary score.
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
last = maximum_nonpadding_index_per_row(sequence)
scores = baseline_empty_handling_or_predict_score(features, last, candidates)

originality.positive: A precise training-only context intervention gives an attributable GRU4Rec experiment tied to observed user complaints.
originality.negative: Sequence cropping is an established augmentation pattern; this application does not support a strong novelty claim.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled result could motivate research into when recurrent recommenders benefit from shorter observed context.
future_potential.negative: Cropping can discard stable preferences and may only act as regularization. Sampled validation improvements would not establish better full-catalog utility.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention changes training examples and target masks while preserving the architecture, checkpoint format and inference computation.
code_difficulty.negative: A valid attribution requires a matched final-target control, careful causal indexing, reproducible sampling and diagnostic-population updates.

related_work.title: UFRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes auxiliary future supervision and contrastive alignment that disappear at inference.
Motivates separating training interventions from deployed scoring architecture.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not demonstrate recent-prefix augmentation or gains on this GRU4Rec benchmark.
Broader future supervision may emphasize persistence rather than immediate intent.

related_work.title: PinnerFormer
contributions: Uses dense future-action supervision to learn persistent user preferences.
limitations: Its architecture and persistent-preference objective differ from the proposed GRU context intervention.
It does not establish that discarding older context improves immediate next-item ranking.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides family-specific ranking objectives and sampling configurations, including BPR-max and cross-entropy.
limitations: Objective recommendations do not identify the cause of the supplied Electronics failures.
Changing objectives alongside cropping would confound the proposed first experiment.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: The supplied search summary distinguishes the always-included positive from sampled negatives in sampled-softmax correction.
limitations: Implementation requires the actual sampling proposal and inclusion semantics.
It offers an alternative objective experiment rather than evidence for context cropping.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of sampled recommendation evaluation and possible changes in model ordering.
limitations: Does not prescribe a model improvement.
The host evaluator remains fixed; conclusions must remain scoped to its pinned protocol.
